title: Properness descends along an arbitrary field extension
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: If X is a scheme over a field k and X_K is proper over K for some field extension K/k, the lemma concludes that X is proper over k (statement lines 2848-2853). The proof first extracts the finiteness conditions from the hypothesis: X_K is separated and quasi-compact, the morphism X_K to X is surjective, so X is quasi-compact, and separating affine opens upstairs shows X is quasi-separated (proof lines 2856-2865). The substantive step is a spreading-out argument: writing K as the colimit of its finitely generated k-subalgebras, the properness of X_K descends to some X_i over Spec(A_i), and a maximal ideal of A_i gives a finite extension k' of k by the Nullstellensatz; base change to k' is then proper, and since k'/k is finite both the projection X_{k'} to X and the composite to Spec(k) are proper, which yields separatedness and then properness of X over k (proof lines 2867-2889). The claim is H2: the descent through a filtered colimit plus the Nullstellensatz reduction to a finite extension is the part that cannot be read off formally.
